name: Content migration from another CMS
scope: Where your client is moving from a CMS other than AEM: inventory the current site with your client, agree which pages to retain, merge or retire, and map each content type to the new site's templates and components. Script the import that builds each retained page on its template, load the pages as content packages through Package Manager, bring their images and files in with Bulk Import, and publish them. Redirect every retired, merged or moved URL through a pipeline-free rewrite map or Dispatcher or CDN rules, and test that old URLs and inbound links reach the agreed pages.
evidence: You can use packages to install new content, transfer content between instances, and back up repository content.

hours_reasoning: Compared with A02 SEO-safe content migration on Edge Delivery (120/240/480), SI03 Content migration with Content Transfer Tool (60/120/240) and AS03 Asset and metadata migration (40/80/200). Adobe documents no import tool for another CMS into a site not on Edge Delivery, so the mapping and import scripts are ours. That puts it about a sixth above A02, which starts from Adobe's importer (though A02 also rewrites SEO copy and this service does not), and well above SI03, which runs on the Content Transfer Tool. Low: one language and a few page types; high: several languages, many page types and a large redirect map.
ext: an Azure Blob Storage or Amazon S3 account to stage images and files for Bulk Import
notes: Written for AEM Sites as a Cloud Service sites not delivered by Edge Delivery Services; every page cited applies to AEM as a Cloud Service. Adobe documents no import tool for another CMS into a site not on Edge Delivery: its content migration FAQ lists the Content Transfer Tool (SI03) and Package Manager for AEM sources and Bulk Import for assets, and the aem.live importer makes content for sites published to Edge Delivery (A02). Adobe's Experience Modernization Agent also moves sites from other CMSes onto Edge Delivery, and its overview (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-cloud-service/content/ai-in-aem/agents/brand-experience/modernization/overview) says: "It does not convert a project to HTL-based publishing or an API-only/SPA delivery stack." So our scripts build the content packages from the old CMS's export, as Adobe's importer does for Edge Delivery sites authored in AEM, and the inventory, mapping and checks are our own practice. Boundaries: SI02 builds the templates and components these pages use; SI08 (new) sets up the language masters and Live Copies a multilingual site moves into; AS03 moves a whole asset library with its metadata, while this service brings in only the images and files the pages use. AS07 (new) then manages those documents' versions, expiry and replacement on the published pages. Flag: SI04's method also agrees 301 redirects for retired URLs at cutover; with both on a statement of work, this service builds and tests the map and SI04 rechecks it on the live site. Adobe's URL redirects page says the CDN configuration file (cdn.yaml) should not exceed 100KB, and its Pipeline-free URL Redirects page calls that approach a good choice when "The number of redirects ranges from a few to tens of thousands." So a large migration map belongs in the rewrite map. Flag: Adobe documents Bulk Import on its AEM Assets pages, while its migration tutorial calls it an AEM as a Cloud Service service; for a client without AEM Assets, the import scripts upload the images and files instead, within these hours. Forms on the old site are not in this scope. For the RFI Builder: on an Edge Delivery RFI, A02 takes SI10's place (add SI10:'A02' to EDS_SIBLING in sow/rfp_answers.js). SI10 is dropped where the RFI moves from AEM 6.x or Adobe Managed Services and names no other CMS, the mirror of keepsLine, which drops SI03 for another CMS. Without both, its CMS-name and content management system phrases outrank A02 on Edge Delivery questions and tie SI03 on AEM 6.5 questions.

steps: Inventory every page and file on your current site with its traffic and inbound links, and agree with your content owners which to retain, merge or retire.
Map each content type to the template and components its pages will use, and write the import scripts that build the pages from that map.
Test the import on each content type with your authors, then load the retained pages in small content packages through Package Manager and their images and files through Bulk Import.
Build the redirect map for every retired, merged or moved URL, load it as a pipeline-free rewrite map or as Dispatcher or CDN redirect rules, and test every entry.
Run the final import after the content freeze and publish it, then check sampled pages against the source, crawl for broken links and test the inventory's inbound links.
deliverables: Page inventory with retain, merge and retire decisions
Published pages, images and files in AEM Sites
Content, link and redirect check report
asks: Export access to your current CMS, plus your site analytics and inbound link data
Content owners who decide which pages to retain, merge or retire, and review samples
A content freeze window agreed with your authors before the final import
method.risk: Pages or links lost in the move: every page is counted against the inventory, and every retired, merged or moved URL is redirected and tested before launch.
method.outcome: Your retained pages are in AEM Sites on their agreed templates, checked against the source, and every old URL and known inbound link reaches the agreed page.
